_about: G11 hardening: deterministic metadata for validating soundwork/tad/project/02_coin.terrificaudio's reconstruction and the beat1/sfx_hit correction. Consumed by soundwork/tad/verify_project.py.
compiler_version_note: The project file's own _about.version field tracks the TAD project-file FORMAT version, independent of the compiler CLI version. An earlier draft of this hardening task assumed the CLI itself was 0.4.2; that version was not found on this machine or in any sibling repo (snes-outrun-sa1, SNES-SuperMonkeyIsland both vendor 0.3.0). Ground truth beats an assumed version number -- see rebuild.py's own comment.

sample_ordering.note: Production is SFX-only; the blank song has no musical instruments.

s02_coin_reconstruction.method: From-scratch bytecode disassembler (grounded in the real audio-driver/src/bytecode.inc source) decoded the shipped s02_coin song's actual note/instrument/timing content from the surviving compiled blob (no original MML/project source ever existed in this repo's history); that was re-encoded to soundwork/tad/project/mml/02_coin.mml.
s02_coin_reconstruction.residual_disposition: Documented in plan_game.md §11 (inherited from the original G11 reconstruction, unchanged by this hardening pass): the 5 residual bytes are isolated to non-melodic echo/pan header settings, not note/instrument/timing content. TAD's MML authoring surface does not expose an exact byte-for-byte echo/pan-register encoding knob for this shape, so these 5 bytes cannot currently be restored exactly from source; they are tracked here so a future build does not silently drift further, per rebuild.py --check.
s02_coin_reconstruction.unaffected_reason: This pass only changed the beat1 BRR-sample entry's pitch model (octave->sample-rate) and its owning SFX bytecode; s0-s6 (the song's own instruments) and mml/02_coin.mml were not touched, so s02_coin's own compiled bytes are unaffected by the beat1/sfx_hit fix.

before.problem: Treated a recorded ~0.379s impact WAV as a pitched musical instrument tuned to an arbitrary 500 Hz reference and truncated playback to 12 SFX ticks (~96ms @ 125 ticks/sec), well short of the source's real length.

after.note: 0 (bare numeric sample-rate-table entry index, not a note name -- sound-effects.txt uses 'play_note 0 48'; TAD's mechanism for a one-shot, non-pitched sample)
after.envelope: gain F127 (flat, unenveloped one-shot -- matches a recorded percussive hit, not adsr note-shaping)
